summary: Iteration 13 verified iter-brief payment edit/reverse + onboarding checklist fixes. Backend: 6/6 pytest PASSED — edit-then-reverse flow on ₹6000 plan (create -> due 6000; pay 2000 -> 4000; edit to 5000 -> 1000; reverse -> 6000 with status Due) with exact number match, edit clamp when amount > payable sets due=0/Paid, PUT/DELETE /payments validation (422 on amount<=0, invalid method, 404 on unknown id), sum(member.due_amount) == finance.summary.outstanding, and onboarding checklist auto-progresses on a fresh registered gym (plan/member/payment/staff flip from false -> true after each creation call), dismiss persists. Frontend web: Payments page shows 20 rows with data-testid payment-edit-* and payment-reverse-*; edit-payment-modal + edit-payment-save render, reverse-payment-modal + reverse-confirm render, record-payment-button present. MemberDrawer -> Transaction History renders per-payment Edit + Reverse (payment-edit-* / payment-reverse-*). Mobile /m: Home shows m-onboarding + m-onboarding-dismiss; Manage -> Members -> tap -> m-action-history opens m-history-list with m-history-edit-* and m-history-reverse-* actions.
action_items: Consider hard-deleting TEST_ prefixed members created by earlier iterations; DELETE /api/members/{id} still leaves them visible in list_members (soft-delete without filter). Not blocking; financial invariants remain intact.

Onboarding self-heal: on demo tenant all 4 steps are marked done, but if a tenant hits GymBoss with legacy data (plans/members exist but flags never set), a one-time backfill on login/tenant load would prevent stale unchecked items. Currently only mutations set the flags.
critical_code_review_comments: _apply_payment_delta adjusts due by (old-new) but does not recompute from sum(payments) — safe under current invariants but drifts if any prior row is inconsistent. Prefer recomputing from db.payments as source of truth on every mutation.

PUT /payments/{id} accepts any positive amount without capping at payable; server clamps due to [0,payable] so revenue and finance stay consistent, but the payment.amount itself can now exceed payable. Consider either rejecting (422) or persisting excess as credit.

Reverse (DELETE) is idempotent-ish but there is no soft-delete/audit-trail on the payment doc itself — hard delete makes forensic recovery impossible; existing audit('payment.reversed') captures the amount but not the full payment doc.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested selectors verified on web + mobile
